To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the variance of the charge in an interval of a 1D system of signed charges is bounded, if and only if the system breaks translation symmetry, and (ii) the variance of a 1d lattice system of charges with values in a bounded subset of the real line is bounded, if the system breaks a discrete translation symmetry.

(i) the boundedness of variance of the total electric charge in an interval of a one-dimensional Coulomb system implies the existence of a nontrivial periodicity in the system; and (ii) the boundedness (in a suitable sense) of the variance of the sum of charges on an interval in a lattice system implies a nontrivial translation symmetry breaking of the corresponding Gibbs measure.

(i) the variance of the charge in an interval in a Coulomb system is bounded if the charges are restricted and (ii) if the average charge density is nontrivial, then the bounded variance implies translation symmetry breaking.
